daily: Exact daily totals and a labeled trailing 7-day mean.
Monthly ticks and rides in thousands show variation through the year.
A muted daily series and thick teal mean avoid competing colors.
Seasonal structure motivates adjustment for month and weekday.
scatter: Warmer dates tend to have more starts
Every point is one date. Pearson r is a descriptive statistic.
The axes show the temperature proxy in °F and starts in thousands.
Small teal dots make overlap visible without obscuring the cloud.
The upward pattern motivates an adjusted comparison.
precip: Fewer starts on measurable precipitation days
All 365 days and group sizes are shown, together with group means.
Recorded zero, trace and measurable days have separate labels.
A common scale and sparse marks keep the comparison readable.
Trace and recorded zero look similar descriptively, while measurable days are lower.
curve: Central 80% of recorded-zero temperatures within each month
Each panel uses its month's observed range and shows pointwise 95% HAC intervals.
Shared axes compare the °F proxy and modeled mean starts across months.
Teal curves and light bands distinguish estimates from uncertainty.
Monthly panels show where the annual model has local temperature support.
residual: Residuals still vary across the year
Adjusted model, ordered by calendar date
All 365 residuals are shown relative to zero.
The time axis helps locate unusual periods and the sign of errors.
A thin baseline and a single data color keep attention on departures.
Runs above and below zero motivate daily dependence checks.
weekday: Daily starts vary by day of week
The line spans the middle 50% of dates, not a confidence interval.
Days follow calendar order and each sample size is printed.
A shared scale and sparse marks make groups easy to compare.
Different day profiles motivate separate weekday controls.
joint: Raw median starts by weather group and temperature band
Sample sizes appear in every cell. Medians are hidden when n < 5.
A common color scale and numerical labels show the median starts.
Muted shading leaves room for the cell labels.
Readers can see which combinations have limited support before interpreting the raw differences.
contrasts: Primary model contrasts, pointwise 95% HAC intervals
All plotted intervals come from the same primary model.
The zero line separates higher from lower modeled starts.
The chart uses one unit and simple interval marks.
Readers can compare magnitudes and distinguish the less precise trace result.
